clue.text: Puzzle a ferocious beast, just over half still to go in

indicators.note: says the partial word is put inside the beast's name

parts.note: a croc, short for crocodile, is a famously ferocious beast

indicators.note: three letters of a five-letter word is just more than half of it, taken from the front

explanation.surface: A cryptic menagerie: a savage animal has only part of something left to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just over half' means three of the five letters of 'still', and 'to go in' says they go inside the beast, not after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A word puzzle whose line initials spell a hidden message is a kind of brain-teaser.

clue.text: Test of popular opinion after upset

indicators.note: after upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A poll that checks public feeling once something has gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters LARO sit across 'popuLAR Opinion'; 'after upset' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination, as opposed to a written paper, is a type of test.

clue.text: Puzzle, cooker not opening

indicators.note: the cooker's name loses its first letter

parts.note: a griddle is a flat plate for cooking on

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by an oven that won't open its door.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum or enigma posed as a question is a classic puzzle.

clue.text: Slight cut in hormone

indicators.note: the word for the slight is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a slight is an insult or snub

explanation.surface: A small reduction in a hormone level, as a doctor might report it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas secretes this hormone to regulate blood sugar.

clue.text: Laid up in house with minor wound for dressing, relax

indicators.note: the wound is dressed, wrapped around the rest

parts.note: a cut is a minor wound

indicators.note: puts the word for laid up within the house abbreviation

parts.note: someone laid up is ill in bed

explanation.surface: An invalid at home with a small injury that needs a bandage tries to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid up' means bedridden, and 'for dressing' casts the wound as the bandage wrapped round everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial phrasal verb for unwinding and taking things easy.

clue.text: 500 more lousy boxes with devious puzzle

indicators.note: the comparative encloses the numeral

parts.note: lousier, that is worse
D is the Roman numeral for 500
arch means sly or devious

explanation.surface: Five hundred inferior containers come with a tricky puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid of letters in which listed terms must be found is a popular puzzle.

clue.text: Notice theme initially in puzzle

indicators.note: places that letter within the puzzle word

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling question

indicators.note: takes the first letter of theme

explanation.surface: Spotting that a crossword's theme shows up at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice pinned on a wall is a printed bill or placard.

clue.text: Shaking rear in defiance, poisoner with toxic tail aggravated, as stinger

indicators.note: shaking off a letter means removing it from the word poisoner
aggravated means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged
takes the last letter of defiance
the tail of toxic is its final letter

explanation.surface: An angry creature raises its venomous tail in defiance, ready to sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaking' drops E (the 'rear in defiance') from POISONER; add C, the 'tail' of toxic, and 'aggravated' rearranges POISONRC.
explanation.definitionFit: An arachnid with a venomous barb at the end of its tail is a stinging creature.

clue.text: Gangster ducks bad luck

parts.note: a hood, short for hoodlum, is a gangster
a duck is a zero score in cricket, so two ducks are two O's

explanation.surface: A mobster keeps dodging misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' looks like a verb (dodges) but gives OO: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinx or run of misfortune, sometimes thought to be caused by a curse.

clue.text: Exhausted after try, back in glee making mark on the field

indicators.note: the word for exhausted comes after the word for try

parts.note: to have a go is to try
all in means worn out

indicators.note: takes the last letter of glee

explanation.surface: A tired player, after scoring a try, returns to celebrations at a rugby ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The white line on a pitch the ball must cross to count as a score.

clue.text: Undoubtedly less relaxation ultimately, after organising two functions

indicators.note: the remaining letters are put in new order
the letters of undoubtedly without that one
takes the final letter of relaxation

explanation.surface: Certainly there's less rest once you start getting things organised.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N (relaxation's last letter, signalled by 'less' and 'ultimately') from UNDOUBTEDLY and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving two purposes at once is an idiom for doing a pair of jobs.

clue.text: Power in old chief

indicators.note: the power letter goes inside the word for old

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A former leader still holding authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chief' is an adjective here: main, principal.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple product or food is the main or principal one.

clue.text: Appropriate force restraining prisoner, immediately aggro starts

indicators.note: the word for force holds the other letters inside

parts.note: to prise something open is to force it
a lag is a convict

indicators.note: takes the opening letters of immediately and aggro

explanation.surface: Guards use force to hold an inmate the moment trouble begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is a verb (to take as your own), not an adjective. PRISE holds LAG plus IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying someone's work and passing it off as yours is taking it wrongfully.

clue.text: Equality of measure turns to misery

indicators.note: the letters turn into a different order

explanation.surface: Fairness in portions soon sours into unhappiness.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry, a transformation preserving distances keeps all measurements equal.

clue.text: Withdraw score

definitions.meaning: to pull out of a race or contest
to mark a surface with a thin line

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are verbs: pulling a horse from a race, and scoring with a claw or nail.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor pulled from an event is scrubbed; a light graze is a scored mark.

clue.text: Line holding up outstanding puzzle

indicators.note: the line holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a cord is a length of line or string

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a debt outstanding is still owed

explanation.surface: A washing line propping up a brilliant puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A word known only to insiders, hiding a meaning, is a kind of cipher.

clue.text: Pull a motor backwards, three times round

indicators.note: the three letters go round the reversed vehicle

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so three of them

indicators.note: the car word is read in reverse

parts.note: a motor is a car

explanation.surface: Towing a car in reverse, three laps of the track.
explanation.walkthrough: T for 'times' is a standard abbreviation; 'round' means the three of them surround the reversed vehicle, with one T split off after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something towards you, as a magnet does, is to exert a pull.

clue.text: Puzzle deception set up

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
to found an institution is to set it up

explanation.surface: Someone baffled on learning a scam was staged.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle or bewilder someone is to leave them perplexed.

clue.text: Proceeds from event finally attributed to composer?

indicators.note: takes the last letter of event

parts.note: belonging to the French composer Maurice Ravel, so Ravel's

explanation.surface: Concert takings credited to a famous musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' looks like a noun (takings) but is the verb: goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey or move along is to go forward, a synonym of proceed.

clue.text: Puzzle has to remain more outrageous

parts.note: to be is to exist or remain, as in let it be
wilder means more extreme or outrageous

explanation.surface: A brain-teaser that must stay even more shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle or confuse someone thoroughly is to perplex them.

clue.text: English team having drawn, no one left

parts.note: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football team

indicators.note: the word for drawn appears with no I in it

parts.note: a side that has drawn has tied
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An English side drew, and nobody stayed behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like part of 'no one left' but is the definition, as a verb: went out.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a room or stage is to go out of it.

clue.text: Puzzle setter cross after local entering error

indicators.note: the cross comes after the rest
the pub abbreviation goes inside the word for error

parts.note: a sin is a wrong or error
PH, public house, is a pub, which Britons call their local
X is a cross

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler is angry after a pub error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle setter' reads like a compiler, but means the mythical creature that set riddles at Thebes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Theban monster posed a riddle to travellers and killed those who failed it.

clue.text: Upstanding partners in supposed special relationship about to complete puzzle

indicators.note: the reversed partners go around the word for complete
in a down entry, standing up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: the UK and the US, said to have a special relationship
to do a task is to complete it

explanation.surface: Two allies in a vaunted friendship stand up, ready to finish a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Partners UK and US are reversed by 'Upstanding' to SUKU, which goes 'about' DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese number-placement grid game is a well-known puzzle.

clue.text: Heated up, warm voice melted heart of model

indicators.note: melted means broken down, so the letters are rearranged
takes the central letter of model

explanation.surface: A model's warm voice melted hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Food zapped in a kitchen oven using radiation has been warmed.

clue.text: Country, capital city once gutted

indicators.note: the city's middle letter is removed

parts.note: Lagos was the capital of Nigeria until 1991

explanation.surface: A nation whose former capital was ripped apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked state in Southeast Asia, bordered by Thailand and Vietnam.

clue.text: See 10
Stunner covering rear in picture puzzle

indicators.note: the stun gun goes around that letter

parts.note: a Taser is a stun gun

indicators.note: takes the last letter of picture

explanation.surface: A beauty covering her backside in a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' suggests a beauty but is the electric weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain-teaser is a tricky problem to solve.

clue.text: Comparing internal material, knife edges cutting through

indicators.note: those letters go into the lining

parts.note: a lining is material on the inside of a garment

indicators.note: takes the first and last letters of knife

explanation.surface: A tailor slicing a coat lining with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing an analogy between two things is equating or comparing them.
